headline: Expertise is deep knowledge in a domain—knowing not just what but why, how, when, and where things work
universal_truth: Depth in one area teaches patterns that apply everywhere; mastering something teaches you how to master anything
fun_facts: Experts see patterns invisible to novices—chess masters recognize board positions in milliseconds
It takes roughly 10 years of focused study to develop true expertise in most fields
Experts organize knowledge differently—in principles and patterns, not just facts
discussion_questions: What are you truly expert in—what do you know deeply?
How did you develop that expertise?
What would you choose to become expert in if you started now?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: An expert doesn't just know more—they see differently. A master mechanic hears problems you don't notice. A skilled doctor sees patterns you'd miss. Expertise is deep knowledge that reorganizes perception itself.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Expertise takes years to develop. In an age of quick information, why pursue deep knowledge?

options.text: Expertise reveals hidden layers—deep knowledge exposes patterns, principles, and connections invisible to surface understanding; it's not just more information but different perception
options.response: Yes. Experts don't just know more facts—they see more reality. Depth changes perception. And the patterns you discover in one domain often transfer to others.
Experience is necessary but not sufficient—expertise requires that experience be analyzed and organized...

q1.title: Pattern Recognition
q1.script: Experts see patterns. Where novices see disconnected facts, experts see organized structures. This pattern recognition enables faster, more accurate decisions.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Pattern Recognition"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Transferable Learning
q2.script: Learning to be expert in one thing teaches you how learning works. The process transfers even when the content doesn't. Mastering something teaches you how to master anything.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Choice of Domain
q3.script: You can't be expert in everything—time is limited. Choosing what to know deeply is strategic. Pick domains that matter to you and leverage well.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Depth in one area teaches patterns that apply everywhere. Mastering something teaches you how to master anything. Pursue depth.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 290. Tomorrow, we'll explore knowing what not to do—constraints. Until then, consider where you'd most benefit from deeper expertise.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Expertise Assessment - What Do You Know Deeply?
growTrack.learning_objective: Evaluate current expertise and plan for development
growTrack.activity: What are you truly expert in—not just familiar with, but deeply knowledgeable about? How did that expertise develop? What additional expertise would be most valuable for your goals?
